mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES remains elevated after a recent dip, commuting-linked foot traffic should recover and pull RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks because more workers create repeat daytime retail demand.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is less negative at t-0w than at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four weeks after WORKPLACES improves for two consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises above its recent average, discretionary trips shift from out-of-home shopping toward staying home, so RETAIL_REC should fall within one week and remain weaker for up to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds its t-2w to t-3w average by at least 1 point
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is flat-to-up across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in the week after RESIDENTIAL crosses above its recent mean.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous upswing in PARKS and TRANSIT indicates broader outbound activity and leisure mobility, which should translate into higher retail-and-recreation visits over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS turns positive at t-0w while TRANSIT is less negative than earlier weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within two weeks when both PARKS and TRANSIT are above their previous two-week averages.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM is stable while TRANSIT remains suppressed, the retail channel is not being reallocated through broad reopening and RETAIL_REC stays below its prior four-week mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -10 for two straight weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is still negative at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-four-week mean despite TRANSIT staying below -10 and GROCERY_PHARM remaining near its recent level.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rebound in PARKS after a negative spell signals substitution toward outdoor leisure rather than retail outings, so RETAIL_REC should weaken over the next one to two weeks as discretionary time shifts away from shopping districts.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from below 0 to above 0
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -1.1 at t-1w to 9.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases after PARKS turns positive and stays positive for at least one weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays positive while WORKPLACES remains below baseline, essential-travel recovery is not broad enough to lift discretionary retail, so RETAIL_REC should remain flat or lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is positive at t-0w while WORKPLACES is negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises for four weeks even though GROCERY_PHARM remains above zero and WORKPLACES stays below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening phase, a rising PARKS series ahead of retail often reflects improving weather and outdoor activity, which should spill into shopping trips and raise RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS shows a strong upward move from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days after PARKS posts a sustained positive weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT recovers enough to approach the less-negative range but WORKPLACES stays weak, travel is likely shifting to non-work trips rather than spending trips, so RETAIL_REC should improve only briefly and then revert lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 4 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES does not improve
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -14.1 at t-1w to -9.3 at t-0w while WORKPLACES stayed negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases for two consecutive weeks after TRANSIT improves despite WORKPLACES remaining depressed.
